name: manual_28a68c
claim: Hand-editing .agent/memory/episodic/AGENT_LEARNINGS.jsonl via a raw Python read-modify-write script, instead of going through the project's own episodic_lock() sidecar-lock mechanism (.agent/harness/hooks/_episodic_io.py), can have its changes silently lost -- a prior dedup pass (34 duplicate rows removed) never actually reached the pushed commit despite an explicit 0-remaining-duplicates verification immediately after running it; the duplicates were already back by the very next commit in git history. The exact concurrent writer was not conclusively identified (auto_dream.py's dream cycle is the only other process documented to rewrite this file via os.replace(), but no direct process/lock evidence was found), but the fix itself -- redoing the dedup while holding episodic_lock() for the full read-modify-write-replace cycle -- is the same protection the project's own code already documents as necessary and that the original dedup skipped
conditions: verify immediately after edit is not enough

decisions.notes: CodeRabbit review #4998833290 on PT PR #359 flagged (correctly, re-confirmed independently) that AGENT_LEARNINGS.jsonl still had all 5 duplicate record groups / 34 duplicate rows after a commit claiming to have deduped them. Traced via git show at each commit: duplicates were present starting at a39d82c7 (the concurrent-branch merge-harmonization commit) and every commit since -- meaning the dedup fix from earlier in the session was lost before or during that merge, most likely because it used an unlocked raw script instead of episodic_lock(), racing against auto_dream.py's documented os.replace()-based rewrite path (its own docstring: 'A sidecar lock is used instead of locking the data inode itself... because the dream cycle rewrites the JSONL file with os.replace'). Verified other memory files (lessons.jsonl: 0 duplicate ids; orama-system has no equivalent episodic/dream-cycle system at all) were not affected by the same class of issue.
